content.content:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

input.command: cd /tmp; curl -si -XPOST localhost:8080/token; echo; T=$(curl -s -XPOST localhost:8080/token | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])'); curl -si -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" 'localhost:8080/orders?page=1' | head -c 1200

content.text:
`result.json` is written in `/workspace`. The by-region figures add up to the total.

- **total_cents:** 9,329,707
- **order_count:** 407
- **duplicates_skipped:** 20
- **by_region:**
  - north: 2,666,579
  - south: 2,714,624
  - east: 1,671,579
  - west: 2,276,925

I fetched all 30 pages, which gave 1,500 listings and 1,480 distinct orders. The 20 repeats are the duplicates, and each order id was counted once.

The date range was applied on UTC time, from 1 March up to but not including 1 June. The status filter was an exact match on "shipped". Each order was discounted and rounded half up individually. No customer lookup returned a 404.

- **Retries:** The service expired the token and rate-limited me partway through. I fetched a fresh token and repeated each failed request after the wait it asked for, so no page was skipped.
- **Retry-After:** The wait time comes in the JSON body (`retry_after`), not in a `Retry-After` header. My script fell back to a 1-second wait, which matched the value the service gave. Anyone writing a client from the docs alone could miss this.

My working script is at `/tmp/work/r.py`, outside the workspace.
